annotations.title: What to fix next, post by post

description: WHAT TO FIX NEXT, post by post, and the tool that fixes it: post_performance says which hook is AHEAD; this says what is WRONG with a post. Under-distributed is A HOOK PROBLEM. Seen but not held is A RETENTION PROBLEM. Seen, held and still not converting is AN OFFER PROBLEM. FOUR REFUSALS, to repeat rather than paper over: (1) a post younger than ~24h is TOO EARLY, never a failure; (2) a metric the platform does not publish is UNMEASURED, never zero (Facebook has published no post reach since 2026-06-15, Reddit publishes no impressions, Google Business nothing per post); (3) below 5 measured posts on a channel there is no brand baseline, and the ONLY fallback is a published short-video hook floor that is NOT our measured number and does not transfer off TikTok/Instagram/YouTube: attribute it as the output does; (4) 'nothing here needs fixing' is a real answer, not a failure to look. Hermoso cannot see conversions for an organic post (no channel reports them against a post id), so the offer rung runs ONLY when the user says they are not converting and you pass converting:false. Print `summary` verbatim. Read-only, 0 credits.

channel.description: restrict to one channel: facebook, instagram, threads, x, linkedin, youtube, tiktok, pinterest, bluesky

converting.description: pass false ONLY when the user has told you these posts are getting seen and are not converting — it re-reads the ones that are earning their reach as an offer problem instead of a win. Omit when you do not know; we cannot measure it.

limit.description: how many recent posts to diagnose (default 25, max 200). The baseline is always built from EVERY post recorded for the brand, never only these, so a bad month can never become its own definition of normal.
